text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as oil prices weakened and refinery margins compressed. U.S. crude dropped to $82.24 per barrel (down sharply from levels earlier in November), while world oil sits at $91.80—a gap that narrows the profit margin refiners earn by processing cheaper domestic crude into products. With refineries already running at a high 97.5% utilization rate and gasoline stocks elevated at 217.7 million barrels, there's limited room for refiners to push volumes higher or command better prices.

The broader headwinds also shifted this week. Collapse of a meaningful climate agreement at COP31 removed near-term regulatory uncertainty that had weighed on oil, but it didn't support prices—instead, it reflected softening global energy demand expectations. Meanwhile, conversations around alternative energy infrastructure (quantum computing for grid optimization, hydrogen catalysts) and investment in non-Russian oil assets suggest longer-term transitions are quietly underway, which can weigh on sentiment around traditional refining even if today's move is driven by crude weakness and margin pressure.
